Reap 12% Interest! – Autauga County, Alabama Tax Lien Investing

Dive into the world of Autauga County, Alabama’s tax lien auctions, where savvy investors can earn up to 12% interest. This online auction system simplifies the process, making it accessible to everyone. By participating in these auctions, you secure a tax lien on properties with unpaid taxes, setting yourself up for potential high returns without directly owning the property.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

In Autauga County, you’re not buying the property itself but rather a tax lien. This means you are paying the back taxes owed on a property, and in return, you can earn interest on your investment. If the property owner redeems the lien, you’ll receive your investment back plus the interest rate you bid. If not, you may have the opportunity to foreclose and gain ownership of the property.

Steps to Start Tax Lien Investing

  1. Research and Understand Local Laws

    Familiarize yourself with Alabama’s tax lien laws to understand your rights and obligations. The key regulations are outlined in the Code of Alabama, Title 40, Chapter 10.
  2. Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

    For detailed tax sale information, visit the Autauga County Revenue/ Reappraisal Office.
  3. Check the Auction Site

    Auctions are held online at GovEase. Register and create an account to start bidding.
  4. Read the Details about Tax Liens

    Visit Autauga County’s Tax Lien Information to learn about the auction schedule, parcel inquiries, and other essential details.
  5. Contact the County Office

    For any questions, reach out to the Autauga County Revenue Commissioner’s Office at (334) 358-6750.

FAQs for Tax Liens

  1. What is a tax lien?

    A tax lien is a claim placed on a property due to unpaid taxes. As an investor, you pay the back taxes and earn interest until the lien is redeemed or you foreclose on the property.
  2. How do I participate in the auction?

    Register on GovEase, create an account, and follow the instructions to participate in the online auction.
  3. What happens if the property owner redeems the lien?

    If the owner pays the owed taxes, you receive your investment back plus the interest you bid.
  4. Can I inspect the properties before bidding?

    Yes, it’s advisable to research and inspect properties before placing a bid.
